seo.description: Extension design and build across Witham, from estate homes to Georgian and timber-framed period property. Planning and building regs handled. Free visit. Call today.

paragraphs: Plenty of people in Witham commute into London and could, in theory, move somewhere bigger. In practice, with fast trains on the doorstep and house prices what they are, most would rather stay and make the home they have work harder. That is the job we do here, more space and a better layout, without the upheaval and cost of moving.
We manage the whole thing as one team, from the design and planning through to the finished room, so you deal with the same people from start to finish.

extensionTypes.intro: Witham's housing is genuinely mixed, and we work across all of it.

planning.title: What the planning usually comes down to
paragraphs: Many extensions in Witham can go ahead under permitted development, but a few local points are worth checking before you plan anything.

The town has two conservation areas: the Georgian High Street around Newland Street, and the older timber-framed core at Chipping Hill, with its green and church. In both, design and materials are judged closely and some permitted development rights fall away, and listed buildings need separate consent. On some of the estates, permitted development rights have been removed by planning condition, so it is worth confirming your house is actually covered rather than assuming it is.

Your authority is Braintree District Council, becoming part of the new North East Essex Council in 2028. Working out which of these applies to your home, and handling the application if one is needed, is our job rather than yours.

ground.title: The ground under Witham
paragraphs: Witham sits on heavy boulder clay, with the River Brain running through the town to meet the Blackwater just outside. That clay holds water, and down in the valley the ground turns soft and, in places, genuinely marshy, digs for the Maltings Lane houses turned up ancient marsh and trackways.

None of that is a problem when it is planned for. It just means foundations and drainage near the river need proper thought, which is why we check the ground early and, on wetter plots, get it investigated before pricing the work.

cost.title: What an extension costs in Witham
paragraphs: Cost comes down to size, specification, structural work and finish, and heavy or wet ground can add to the groundwork.

As a rough guide, single-storey extensions commonly run at a few thousand pounds per square metre, with double storey often better value per square metre. That is a starting point, not a quote. Our cost calculator gives an early estimate, and a free site visit gives you a real, itemised figure.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for an extension in Witham?
faqs.a: Often not, but it depends on your home. The Newland Street and Chipping Hill conservation areas reduce permitted development rights, listed buildings need separate consent, and some estates have those rights removed by planning condition. We check your exact address with Braintree District Council and handle any application.

faqs.q: Do you work on period and timber-framed homes?
faqs.a: Yes. Witham has elegant Georgian houses on Newland Street and timber-framed homes around Chipping Hill, and we extend and renovate them sympathetically, matching materials and handling listed building consent where it applies.

faqs.q: Why does the local ground matter for my foundations?
faqs.a: Witham sits on heavy boulder clay, with soft and sometimes marshy ground down in the River Brain valley. That affects both foundations and drainage, so we check it before starting rather than meeting it mid-build.
